strings.name: El Anatsui
strings.summary: El Anatsui is a Ghanaian artist who taught and worked for decades in Nigeria. Using aluminum liquor-bottle caps and copper wire, he creates metal sculptures whose forms can change with installation. His practice also encompasses clay, wood and printmaking, connecting reuse with trade, colonial histories and consumption. He conceives the works and collaborates with a studio team to make them.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Ghanaian identity, Nigerian career, commissions, prizes and creation/acquisition dates are distinguished. Future exhibitions are recorded as announcements; exhibitions or sales do not prove personal attendance.
strings.influence.rationale: Connects African craft, trade history and global consumption through recycled metal and mutable installations, expanding the international impact of material-based art.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education and teaching
strings.facts.f1.value: His CV lists a KNUST bachelor’s course completed in 1968 and a postgraduate diploma in art education in 1969. He joined the University of Nigeria in 1975; the professorship is dated 1996–2011.
strings.facts.f2.label: Form and materials
strings.facts.f2.value: Folded and flattened aluminum caps are joined with copper wire. The works resemble fabric but are metal sculptures that can be reshaped during installation.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Histories carried by materials
strings.highlights.h1.text: Uses discarded objects to question consumption, trade and colonial exchange; his practice includes clay, wood, printing plates and prints as well as bottle caps.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Collaboration and non-fixed form
strings.highlights.h2.text: Assistants construct linked units, the artist develops compositions, and installation changes the work further; studio labor and formal flexibility remain visible.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Philadelphia print exhibition announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: The museum announces Prints and Play for December 19, 2026–May 2, 2027; it had not opened at the cutoff.
strings.timeline.t2.title: MivEvi opens in Hong Kong
strings.timeline.t2.text: White Cube presents new double-sided metal works through May 9, exploring orientation and relationships between surfaces.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Behind the Red Moon opens at Tate
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Hyundai Commission unfolds as a three-act installation in the Turbine Hall through April 14, 2024; a commission, not a competitive prize.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Receives Praemium Imperiale for sculpture
strings.timeline.t4.text: The Japan Art Association presents the sculpture award in Tokyo.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Receives Venice Biennale Lifetime Achievement Golden Lion
strings.timeline.t5.text: The 56th International Art Exhibition honors his lifetime achievement, distinct from national-pavilion or film awards.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Creates Between Earth and Heaven
strings.timeline.t6.text: The Met records aluminum and copper wire, created in 2006 and acquired in 2007; the dates remain distinct.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Moves to Nigeria to teach
strings.timeline.t7.text: Joins the University of Nigeria in Nsukka, continuing sculpture and teaching; he did not graduate from KNUST that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes postgraduate diploma in art education
strings.timeline.t8.text: After his 1968 bachelor’s course, receives the KNUST diploma and begins teaching in Winneba; it is not a doctorate.
